The input to the algorithm is a single number: the positive integer \(d\). This algorithm has been used to classify smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes for \(d \leq 7\). The authors present an algorithm for generating the classification list of smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes in any prescribed dimension \(d\). The method is designed to be general: its only required input is the positive integer \(d\), representing the dimension in which the classification is to be carried out.

Using this algorithm, the authors have classified smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes for all dimensions \(d \leq 7\). Their results include a complete list of isomorphism classes in these dimensions. In particular, the classification contains 7,622 isomorphism classes of smooth Fano 6-polytopes and 72,256 isomorphism classes of smooth Fano 7-polytopes.
outputs.L4:
We present an algorithm for the classification of smooth Fano polytopes in arbitrary fixed dimension. For any positive integer \(d\), the algorithm takes only \(d\) as input and produces, up to lattice isomorphism, all smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes. Here a smooth Fano polytope is a full-dimensional lattice polytope whose vertices are primitive lattice points, whose interior contains the origin, and whose facets correspond to lattice bases. Such polytopes are of central importance in toric geometry, since they correspond to smooth toric Fano varieties.

The method provides a systematic and finite procedure for constructing all possible candidates and eliminating duplicates under lattice isomorphism. In this way, the classification problem is reduced to an explicit computation depending only on the dimension. The algorithm extends earlier classification methods and makes it possible to treat dimensions beyond those previously known.

We implemented the algorithm and applied it to dimensions up to \(7\). The computation reproduces the known classifications in lower dimensions and yields new classification data in higher dimensions. In particular, we found \(7{,}622\) isomorphism classes of smooth Fano polytopes in dimension \(6\), and \(72{,}256\) isomorphism classes in dimension \(7\). These results extend the previously known classification of smooth Fano polytopes and provide a complete list in these dimensions.

counterfactuals.output:
The paper’s main result is a **general finite algorithm** that, for any fixed dimension \(d\), produces the complete classification of **smooth Fano polytopes** up to lattice isomorphism.

Equivalently, it gives an effective way to enumerate all smooth toric Fano varieties of dimension \(d\). The algorithm exploits the existence of special facets and strong combinatorial bounds on the vertices of a smooth Fano polytope, reducing the classification to a finite, computable search.

In the paper, the algorithm is also implemented to obtain explicit classifications in low dimensions—most notably extending the known lists up to dimension \(7\), where there are \(72{,}256\) smooth Fano polytopes.

counterfactuals.prompt: What does the classification algorithm for smooth Fano d-polytopes do, and how many isomorphism classes are known for d ≤ 7?
counterfactuals.output:
The classification algorithm for smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes (often associated with Øbro’s algorithm) systematically enumerates all smooth Fano polytopes up to lattice isomorphism.

In broad terms, it does the following:

1. **Uses a “special facet”**: every smooth Fano polytope has a facet whose vertex sum satisfies strong constraints.
2. **Chooses coordinates relative to that facet**: the facet vertices can be taken as a lattice basis.
3. **Bounds the possible remaining vertices**: smoothness and the Fano condition force all other vertices to lie in a finite, explicitly computable set.
4. **Enumerates candidate vertex sets** from this finite set.
5. **Tests the candidates** for being smooth Fano polytopes: full-dimensional, origin in the interior, primitive vertices, and every facet giving a lattice basis.
6. **Removes duplicates up to lattice isomorphism**, i.e. up to unimodular transformations in \(\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb Z)\).

The known numbers of isomorphism classes of smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes for \(d \le 7\) are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
d & \#\text{ smooth Fano } d\text{-polytopes} \\
\hline
1 & 1 \\
2 & 5 \\
3 & 18 \\
4 & 124 \\
5 & 866 \\
6 & 7622 \\
7 & 72256
\end{array}
\]

So for dimensions \(d \le 7\), there are \(72{,}256\) isomorphism classes in dimension \(7\), and the cumulative total through dimension \(7\) is \(80{,}892\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
